text:
Matvei Michkov spent the weekend as the most talked-about player in Philadelphia, for a reason no young star wants: headlines about his ice time, including Broad Street Hockey's "Matvei Michkov sends clear message to Flyers about limited ice time." On Monday in Vancouver he played 15:24, set up a power-play goal and was named first star of a 3-1 win that ended the Flyers' three-game winless run (0-2-1). One night settles nothing, but it was the right night to have.

The Flyers had this one under control for 40 minutes. Michael Bunting scored 2:03 in, from Christian Dvorak and Nick Seeler, and Travis Konecny made it 2-0 on the power play at 3:05 of the second with Michkov and Dvorak assisting. Philadelphia won both of those periods on expected goals, the quality of the chances, 0.97 to 0.29 and 0.88 to 0.33. Dvorak finished with two assists and the second star.

Then the third happened. Vancouver took over, and Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports counted the Flyers' shot attempts in the period on one hand. The best chance that didn't go in was still Philadelphia's, a 37 percent look for Michael Bunting that Leevi Meriläinen stopped. Jonathan Lekkerimäki, skating with Elias Pettersson and Brock Boeser, scored on the power play at 12:44 to make it 2-1, and Joseph Woll's biggest save came on Lekkerimäki again later in the period. The night also produced what Pass it to Bulis's Daniel Wagner called "the extremely rare 'Goalie removed own mask' minor." Travis Sanheim ended it at 19:01, a shorthanded shot into the empty net with the Canucks playing six on four, per O'Connor.

Our numbers call it a coin flip: 50 percent deserved to win each way, with Woll (18 of 19, 1.26 goals saved above expected) the difference. "It's a win, but after that third period, it really doesn't feel like one," O'Connor posted. In Vancouver the mood was worse. CanucksArmy's Wyatt Arndt headlined "Canucks offer up pathetic effort in 3-1 loss to Rick Tocchet's Flyers." We'd say the chances were closer than that, but the Canucks are now winless in six (0-6-0), and close stopped being much comfort a while ago.
headline: Michkov stars as Flyers survive a shaky third
